$comment: D-CPP-ERROR-WARNING (C23 6.10.5 `#error` / 6.10.6 `#warning`) runtime witness. ★ WHY THIS EXISTS: the unit tests stop at the DiagnosticReporter -- none of them reaches past it into the real driver + spawn, so nothing else pins the property that MAKES `#warning` usable: a Warning-severity PREPROCESSOR diagnostic must let the build PROCEED through compile -> link -> RUN. The LIVE `#warning` here is `sys/cdefs.h:81` verbatim (`#if !defined(__GNUC__)` is TRUE -- DSS predefines __STDC__ but not __GNUC__), i.e. the advisory the Apple SDK header greets a non-gcc compiler with on nearly every macOS TU. It fires as warning[P001F] during this example's compile and the binary still links, spawns and exits 42. RED-ON-DISABLE (headline): emitting `#warning` at Error severity -- drop the explicit `DiagnosticSeverity::Warning` argument from the `#warning` `emitPP` (every other `emitPP` in preprocessor.cpp DEFAULTS to Error) -- fails the build → no binary → this example reds. Secondarily, three dead `#error`s ride along as C 6.10p1 reachability coverage, one per conditional form (`#if 0`, `#ifdef DSS_NEVER_DEFINED`, a not-taken `#else`): a regressed dead-branch gate -- hoisting the `#error` arm above `if (!stackActive()) return end;` -- turns any of the three into a hard compile failure (P001E is Error severity AND unsuppressable), again with no binary to run. A mis-evaluated live guard instead takes the `#else` arm (BASE=0 -> exit 2). BASE/MARGIN reach add() as function args so the baseline arm keeps a live runtime add (not const-folded to an immediate at exit), and the optimizedPipelines `release` arm runs the SHIPPED pipeline over the same source.
